item.title: I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Obioma Ofoegbu has spoken about the challenges of being stereotyped because of her plus-size physique, saying she is determined to establish herself as a versatile performer capable of taking on diverse roles. In an interview with Potpourri, Ofoegbu said she had repeatedly been offered roles that portrayed her as an older woman or confined her to characters typically associated with plus-size actresses. “My biggest challenge when I started was not being stereotyped because of my body type. A lot of times, they tried to give me roles just because I’m a plus-size woman. They would make me older in some movies or give me the same stories that a plus-size woman is expected to tell,” she said. The actress, who officially began her film career in 2020 after years of participating in stage plays and theatre productions during her school days, said she had rejected several roles in a bid to break away from such limitations. “I’m young. I don’t have to play an older woman or a married woman just because I’m plus-size. I don’t want to be placed in a box because of my looks, my appearance, or where I live,” she added. Speaking about her most challenging role, Ofoegbu identified her performance in Africa Magic’s series, The Low Priest, where she portrayed a villainous character who undergoes a transformation. She described the experience as physically demanding, revealing that she had to learn more Igbo, chant incantations and endure challenging filming conditions. The experience, she said, strengthened her confidence in her abilities and taught her that preparation and resilience could help her handle demanding characters. Despite her preference for diverse roles, Ofoegbu admitted that economic realities in Nigeria could make accepting stereotypical roles necessary, particularly for emerging actors trying to establish themselves financially. “I’m not a Funke Akindele yet. I’m not big enough to be producing as I please, so definitely I would take up those roles. I would grow as an actor, save, build and get my face out there,” she said. She also described acting as an uncertain source of income for emerging performers, advising actors to develop alternative income streams rather than depend entirely on film roles. On film promotion, the actress, who also has experience as an executive producer, maintained that actors should support projects they feature in but insisted that producers must have independent marketing strategies. Her long-term ambition, she said, is to have her work recognised beyond Africa and collaborate with filmmakers across different parts of the world. “I’m an actor, I’m not just a Nollywood actor. I like to see myself as an actor. Nollywood is a starting point for me,” she said. The post I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cut ties with ungrateful people, disloyal family members – Titilola Ajayi
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Rising actress and filmmaker, Titilola Ajayi, popularly known as Omoposh and known for her movie Mr and Mrs Parker, has stressed the importance of setting personal boundaries, urging people not to tolerate disrespect, exploitation or emotional manipulation, even from family members. Ajayi made this known in a recent post on her Instagram page, where she addressed the need to walk away from relationships with ungrateful people and disloyal family members. According to her, family relationships should never be used as an excuse to endure mistreatment. “Clear boundaries are important and honestly cutting ties with ungrateful people or disloyal family members is also valid. Family should never be an excuse to tolerate disrespect, exploitation or emotional manipulation,” she wrote. She also had a message for people who continue to show kindness, generosity and support to others despite unpleasant experiences. “To all the good hearted people who give , support and show up for others don’t let experiences change your beautiful heart. Continue to be kind but learn to set boundaries . You can have a good heart and still know when to cut off ingrates and walk away,” she added. item.title: Nollywood must stop choosing Instagram numbers over talent – Uche Montana
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Uche Montana has questioned the Nigerian movie industry’s growing emphasis on social media popularity over acting ability, insisting that talent should remain an important consideration in the selection of actors. She shared her thoughts during an interview with media personality Davibes Olamide, where she also discussed friendship, fame, success and the realities of celebrity life. Speaking about the industry’s preference for social media numbers, she said: “The Nigerian movie industry needs to stopnpicking numbers on Instagram over talent” The actress also shared her thoughts on the relationship between friendship and success. Asked if she would pursue success even if it meant losing her friends, Montana responded: “Without my friends would i be broke ?Because I don’t want to be broke” She further explained her position on the value of genuine friendship, stating: “You can’t quantify friendship with the things of the world . Because good friendship means the world” Addressing the misconceptions surrounding celebrity life, Montana identified the belief that celebrities receive things for free as one of the biggest lies about fame. “The biggest lie about being a celebrity is that you get things for free” She also pointed out that certain things remain beyond the reach of fame, saying: “One thing fame can’t buy is peace good health” On the subject of respect and personal value, she observed: “People only respect you when you have value” The post Nollywood must stop choosing Instagram numbers over talent – Uche Montana appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Odumodublvck set to make acting debut in TG Omori’s ‘The Rise of the Machine’
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Multi-award-winning rapper Odumodublvck is showcasing his artistic depth with a stellar performance in his acting debut in a short film directed by ace cinematographer TG Omori. On November 7 2026, rapper Odumodublvck and cinematographer TG Omori were special guests at the closing ceremony and award gala of the 15th Africa International Film Festival ( AFRIFF), where they screened their short film titled ‘The Rise of the Machine’. The film, directed by celebrated cinematographer TG Omori, who is famous for shooting some of Africa’s most iconic music videos of the past decade, will see Odumodublvck make his acting debut in a role that promises to unleash another dimension to his talent and creativity. Speaking on the short film in a recent interview on TVC, the rapper described it as an addendum to his recently acclaimed projects, ‘The Machine is Coming’ and ‘The Industry Machine’. On making his acting debut, the award-winning rapper shared that he has enjoyed acting from a young age and always wanted to showcase that talent. “Since I was in primary and secondary school, I was in drama club. And with movies, I can show a lot more than listening to my music might show.” The short film is a precursor to the release of his upcoming project of the same name, which will complete his Machine Trilogy. The first instalment, ‘The Machine Is Coming’ enjoyed huge commercial success with the hits ‘Legolas’ and ‘Pity This Boy’ featuring Victony. The album was recently nominated for the Best Rap Album and Album of the Year at the 18th Headies. The follow-up, ‘The Industry Machine,’ also spawned chart-topping records with the hit single ‘Industry Machine’ and the hip hop anthem ‘If You Like Gym,’ which earned the nod for Best Rap Single at the 16th Headies. ‘The Rise of the Machine’ was shot in Lagos State and marks a major chapter in the career of Omori, who will be making his movie directorial debut and Odumodublvck, who serves as co-producer and executive producer. The short film is scheduled for release later in 2026 ahead of Odumodublvck’s new project, which will complete his Machine Trilogy while also kicking off his career as an actor and filmmaker. item.title: Australian pop singer, Nishka set to make Lagos performance debut
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Australian pop singer, Nishka, is set to make her Lagos performance debut as a special musical guest at Escape, an upcoming art exhibition that will bring music and contemporary visual art together in Lagos on November 28, 2026. The Melbourne-based singer’s appearance at the exhibition, organised by visual artist Fortune Ileleji and Grammy-winning musician Tejiri Sonics, is expected to add an international dimension to the creative experience while introducing Nigerian audiences to Nishka’s distinctive blend of soulful vocals, contemporary pop and rhythm-driven production. For Nishka, the Lagos performance represents more than another appearance on the international music calendar. It marks the latest stage in the journey of an artist whose sound has been shaped by multiple cultures, genres and experiences. Raised in Melbourne, Australia, in a family of Macedonian heritage, Nishka grew up surrounded by soul, funk, hip-hop and house music, alongside the traditional sounds of her family background. Those influences would eventually become part of the musical foundation from which she developed her own identity in pop. Her journey into music began early. At 10, Nishka started singing while simultaneously taking up martial arts. For several years, she pursued both disciplines, competing in martial arts tournaments while developing her vocal ability. By the age of 15, however, she had made a decisive choice: music would become her life’s pursuit. Today, Nishka’s music combines a soulful voice with emotional storytelling and a strong rhythmic character. Her songs explore love, desire, vulnerability and self-discovery, shifting between intimate, emotionally charged moments and energetic, groove-driven sounds. Her debut single, On My Mind, offers an introduction to that musical identity, blending personal expression with a contemporary pop sound. The choice of an art exhibition as the setting for her first Nigerian performance is also significant. Music and visual art, though expressed through different mediums, often meet at the same point—the attempt to translate emotions, memories and experiences that words alone cannot fully capture. That intersection is at the heart of Escape. The exhibition will bring together the visual work of Fortune Ileleji and Tejiri Sonics, with Nishka’s live performance adding a musical layer to the experience and creating a platform where contemporary art and international pop music converge. For the organisers, the appearance of an Australian-based artiste also underscores the increasingly interconnected nature of the creative industries, where artists, audiences and cultural influences now move across borders with greater ease. For Nishka, Lagos offers another cultural setting in which to expand an artistic identity already built from different musical traditions. item.title: My appearance has helped with visibility, branding — DJ Pretty Smile
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Sexy and beautiful Nigerian disc jockey, Onyinyechi Maureen Eneje, popularly known as DJ Pretty Smile, has admitted that her physical appearance has played a significant role in boosting her visibility and personal branding, even as she insists that talent and performance remain the key to sustaining a successful career. The beautiful DJ, who made the revelation in an interview with Potpourri, said her personality and appearance often attract people’s attention initially, but her ability to deliver behind the decks is what keeps them interested. According to her, being a woman in a male-dominated entertainment industry comes with its advantages in terms of visibility, but appearance alone cannot guarantee longevity in the profession. “I think people are first attracted to my personality and appearance, but what keeps them interested is my energy and ability to actually deliver behind the decks. Being a woman in a male-dominated space definitely makes people notice you, but looks alone cannot sustain a career. You have to be good at what you do,” she said. She added that although her appearance has contributed to her visibility and branding, she wants to be recognised primarily for her musical abilities and capacity to entertain audiences. “My appearance has definitely helped with visibility and branding, but I’ve always wanted people to remember me as DJ Pretty Smile, the DJ who can actually make a room move,” she added. Speaking on why she chose disc jockeying over singing or dancing, Eneje said her passion for music and its ability to influence people’s moods informed her decision to become a DJ. “I’ve always loved music and the way it can change people’s mood instantly. I chose DJing because I love being the person who controls that energy and creates an experience for people,” she explained. She further described disc jockeying as more than simply playing songs, noting that the profession requires an understanding of audiences, timing and the ability to establish a connection with people. “For me, it’s not just about playing songs; it’s about knowing what people want to hear, when they want to hear it, and creating that connection with the crowd. I also love the freedom and creativity that comes with DJing,” she said. On the argument that disc jockeys do not receive the recognition and financial rewards commensurate with their contributions to the music industry, DJ Pretty Smile agreed that the concern was justified to some extent. She observed that DJs play an important role in promoting songs and introducing music to wider audiences, but their contributions are not always adequately recognised or rewarded. “To some extent, yes. DJs play a huge role in the music industry because we help introduce and push songs to audiences, but sometimes the recognition and financial rewards don’t reflect the value we bring,” she stated. item.title: I don’t just want a relationship, I want something meaningful – Peju Johnson
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Peju Johnson says her priorities in love and career have changed as she grows older, stressing that she is no longer interested in relationships merely for the sake of being in one but desires a meaningful union built on genuine love, peace, friendship and mutual understanding. The actress, who attracted attention on social media on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, as she celebrated her birthday with stunning photographs, made this known in a chat with *Potpourri*, where she reflected on her journey in the movie industry, personal struggles, love life and aspirations for the future. According to Johnson, her experiences in the entertainment industry have taught her patience, resilience and the importance of self-belief, particularly in an environment where not everyone who appears supportive genuinely wishes others well. “The film industry has taught me patience, resilience and the importance of believing in myself, even when nobody else sees the vision,” she said. “I’ve learnt that not everybody who smiles with you genuinely wants to see you win, and that’s okay. You must learn to protect your peace, stay focused and never allow people’s opinions to define your worth.” Speaking about her changing expectations in relationships as she advances in age, the actress said she now places greater value on emotional stability, intentionality and personal growth than simply having a romantic partner. “As I grow older, my priorities are becoming clearer. In my love life, I want peace, genuine love, friendship, understanding and a partner who is intentional. “I’m at a stage where I don’t just want to be in a relationship for the sake of being in one. I want something meaningful, something that adds value to my life and allows both of us to grow. “I want to love and be loved without losing myself in the process,” she stated. Beyond her expectations in love, Johnson said she is equally concerned about building a career and legacy that would extend beyond her achievements as an actress. She explained that her ambition goes beyond being recognised as an actress and producer, noting that she hopes to establish herself as a filmmaker and businesswoman capable of creating opportunities for others. “Career-wise, my major concern is building something that will outlive me. I don’t just want to be known as an actress and producer; I want to build a lasting legacy as a filmmaker, producer and businesswoman. “I want to create opportunities, tell meaningful stories and establish something that the next generation can benefit from,” she added. item.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. item.title: Denmark hammer Ronaldo-less Portugal 4-1 in Nations League match
item.description: Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football. Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga. The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures. A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through. Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys. Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches. The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September. That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked liked they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display. Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile’s Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute. Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shellshocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area. Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time. Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brook’s chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B. item.title: Obasanjo urges Nigerian youths to shun divisive, discriminatory campaigns
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has called on Nigerian youths to shun campaign of division, segregation, discrimination and marginalisation. Obasanjo made the call on Saturday after receiving an honorary doctorate degree conferred on him by the Skyline University of Nigeria in Kano. He was conferred with the honour alongside former Executive Secretary, National Universities Commission (NUC), Prof. Abubakar Adamu-Rasheed and Mrs. Vadana Luthra. The former president, who addressed the gathering through a recorded video, said the youths, irrespective of their tribe, religion and age, must be the architects of their own future and fortune, noting they have to struggle for what they want, as salvation will not come from heaven. He said himself, and the late Head of State Murtala Muhammad spearheaded the change in the country. Obasanjo said the youths have to be positively disruptive to bring about the desired change. “Most of the leaders of the immediate, pre and post-independent era were young and active. “They went for change, and they made it happen. Nigeria, as a whole, benefited from their activism. “Let me name two – Aminu Kano and Enahoro. The military era was not much different.” Earlier, the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Ajith Kumar, announced approval of new programmes by the National Universities Commission (NUC), adding that the university was the first in North-West Nigeria to receive approval for the B.Sc. Artificial Intelligence programme. He said the development further demonstrates its commitment to advancing technology-driven education in the region. Kumar said the institution has awarded a 50% scholarship to all toppers to pursue their postgraduate programmes at the university. A total of 237 students graduated with various degrees at the institution’s 5th convocation ceremony. (NAN) The post Obasanjo urges Nigerian youths to shun divisive, discriminatory campaigns appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Atiku Promises To Resume Oil Exploration In Kolmani, Revive Mabilla Power Project
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has promised to resume oil exploration activities at the Kolmani oil field, which he said were suspended under the present administration. He also pledged to restore electricity subsidies and revive work on the abandoned Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project in the North-East. ﻿ Atiku made these promises during his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State on Saturday. Speaking at the rally, he said, “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue.” On his part, Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign, Mr. Austin Akobundu, criticised what he described as the poor governance and misguided policy decisions of the present administration. “There is hunger in the land, and the man who will eradicate it is Atiku,” he said. item.title: 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno
item.description: Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, saying that he will back any coalition that supports President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Eno stated this while fielding questions during a media chat on Saturday. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the President,” he said. “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am for it.” The governor said that the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom is “good on the ground”. Eno, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC after his defection from the PDP in June 2025, said the two parties had agreed to support Tinubu, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and himself in the 2027 general elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to PDP-APC relationship,” the governor said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the President, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” The Rainbow Coalition is spearheaded by Wike to galvanise support for the re-election bid of President Tinubu in 2027. But the coalition has faced opposition from leaders of the APC. In October, 2026, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma said that the Rainbow Coalition has no presence in the state. Speaking during the distribution of campaign vehicles under the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state, Uzodimma insisted that the APC would secure victory in the 2027 elections through organic votes. The governor maintained that the APC was the only recognised political party in the state and urged supporters to vote for the party’s candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Similarly, Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal told the minister to make his political position clear over his involvement with the coalition, insisting that he cannot simultaneously support the APC and other political parties. “Our message is very, very clear: be on one side, you can’t be on two sides. If you are in APC, please come out and support the APC, not you are supporting APC here, and you are supporting some other political parties somewhere else,” he said during an interview with Channels Television’s Inside Sources on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York in October. item.title: FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash
item.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Anambra State Sector Command, has confirmed one death and eight injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash at Agu-Awka, Immigration Junction, along the Awka-Enugu Expressway. The sector commander, Corps Commander Bridget Asekhauno, personally led the rescue efforts following the crash. Asekhauno told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday that the crash occurred at about 8.45 a.m. and involved a Sinotruck trailer, a Toyota Camry and a TVS commercial tricycle. She said that the vehicles had registration numbers AAA920YN, ENU622DR and NSH684VC, respectively. “Preliminary investigations indicated excessive speeding and inadequate construction warning signs as suspected factors responsible for the crash. “An eyewitness account indicated that the trailer, while descending a slope, noticed a diversion sign and attempted to manoeuvre into another lane. “The trailer reportedly collided sideways with the Toyota Camry, which subsequently hit the tricycle from behind, while the trailer somersaulted,” she said. The sector commander said that nine persons were involved in the crash, with one confirmed dead and eight sustained varying degrees of injuries. She added that five of the injured victims were taken to hospital for medical attention. According to her, the FRSC rescue team promptly mobilised to the scene to manage traffic and clear the obstruction. “The prompt intervention ensured the clearance and reopening of the blocked diversion route to motorists,” she said. Asekhauno expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. She urged construction companies to provide adequate and visible warning signs, particularly around construction zones and diversion points, to guide motorists and prevent avoidable crashes. She also advised motorists to observe speed limits, exercise caution around diversions and construction areas as well as pay attention to road signs and traffic instructions. The sector commander reiterated FRSC’s commitment to prompt emergency response, effective traffic management and the protection of lives and property on Nigerian roads. (NAN) The post FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain
item.description: Super Eagles forward Ademola Lookman has been ruled out of Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying return-leg fixture against Tanzania following a knee ligament sprain. Promise Efoghe, Super Eagles Media Officer, confirmed the development to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday. “Scan has revealed Ademola Lookman suffered a sprain in his knee ligament during yesterday’s match. “This rules him out of Nigeria’s next AFCON qualifier against Tanzania in Zanzibar on Tuesday,” Efoghe said. The injury was sustained during Nigeria’s 3-1 victory over Tanzania in their Matchday Three encounter at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday. Lookman’s absence will be a setback for the Super Eagles as they prepare for the return fixture against the Taifa Stars. The Athletico Madrid forward has been an important attacking option for Nigeria, providing creativity, pace and goal-scoring threat in the final third. NAN reports that Friday’s victory strengthened Nigeria’s position in the qualifying campaign, taking their points tally to six. The Super Eagles will now travel to Zanzibar for Tuesday’s Matchday Four encounter, hoping to consolidate their position in the group. Nigeria will be seeking another positive result against Tanzania as the race for qualification for the 2027 AFCON finals gathers momentum. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are already guaranteed places at the tournament as co-hosts, leaving the remaining qualification spots to be contested by other countries. The 2027 AFCON finals will be jointly hosted by the three East African countries. (NAN) The post Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Soludo demands reopening of Anambra court of appeal
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for the immediate reopening of the Court of Appeal in the state, arguing that the volume of litigation generated by Anambra, which he said is second only to Lagos, justifies its continued operation. Soludo made the demand during a church service marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year of the Anambra State Judiciary. He also urged the Nigerian legal profession to abandon imported wigs and gowns in favour of locally produced alternatives, saying the continued importation of legal attire amounts to exporting employment opportunities that could be created in Nigeria. The special service was presided over by the Bishop of Aguata, Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province on the Niger, Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor. It was attended by judicial officers, legal practitioners and government functionaries. Addressing the gathering, Soludo reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving justice delivery but expressed concern over the continued closure of the Court of Appeal in Anambra. “Anambra, after Lagos, generates more cases. We are more deserving to have the Court of Appeal. “The Court of Appeal in Anambra should not be closed for one day if merit and need happen to be the criteria. Come and open your court,” he said. The governor also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the welfare of judicial officers and the provision of necessary infrastructure for the judiciary. He noted that the state’s plea-bargaining initiative was helping to decongest correctional facilities. On the need to promote local industries, Soludo challenged lawyers and judicial officers to embrace Nigerian-made legal attire rather than continue importing wigs and gowns. “Can we change the law regalia into what is made in Nigeria? We are creating jobs abroad by importing all the regalia you wear. “Let us eat what we produce and wear what we make. That is the way to help the economy. I wear Akwete to promote Made-in-Nigeria,” he said. The governor, who is known for wearing Akwete fabric, said adopting locally produced materials would support domestic industries and create employment opportunities. On security, Soludo highlighted the cooperation among the executive, legislature and judiciary, crediting the state’s Homeland Security Law with strengthening the security architecture and restoring calm in different parts of Anambra. “We may have different branches of government, but we have one objective: the security and welfare of Ndi Anambra,” he said. Addressing the crisis within the Awka Diocese of the Anglican Communion, the governor said his administration had maintained neutrality, describing the dispute as a private affair of the Anglican Church in Anambra and Nigeria. item.title: Don’t disappoint Nigeria’s founding fathers, Jonathan warns political leaders
item.description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria’s political leaders to rebuild the country, warning against disappointing the founding fathers. This ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‍​‌‌​is contained in a statement issued by the former president’s Media Adviser, Mr Ikechukwu Eze, in Abuja on Saturday. Eze quoted Jonathan as making the call while delivering his address at a colloquium organised in honour of the 162nd birth anniversary of a nationalist, Pa Herbert Macaulay, at Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos on Saturday. Jonathan, who was the chairman of the occasion, challenged Nigeria’s political leaders and citizens to reflect on whether the country had lived up to the dreams and aspirations of its founding nationalists. He asked whether Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and other heroes of the independence struggle would be proud of today’s Nigeria or regret the outcome of their sacrifices. Speaking on the theme “Nationalism and Nation Building”, the former president said the vision of Nigeria’s founding nationalists went beyond the transfer of political power from colonial authorities to Nigerians. “They envisaged a sovereign, united and prosperous country where citizens would enjoy equal rights, economic opportunities, quality education, accessible healthcare and the benefits of accountable governance,” he said. Jonathan appealed that Nigeria must not allow its founding nationalists to regret the struggle they waged for independence. According to him, the greatest tribute to the nation’s heroes is not merely to celebrate their birthdays or preserve their monuments but to build a country that reflects the ideals for which they sacrificed. “We must not make Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and the other founding nationalists regret, even in their graves, the struggle they waged for our independence,” he said. Jonathan urged the present generation to ensure that today’s national challenges were not allowed to become the inheritance of their children and grandchildren. He expressed concern that 66 years after independence, Nigeria had yet to substantially realise many of these aspirations. According to him, while Nigeria has recorded progress in several areas, patriotism demands the courage to confront its shortcomings, including leadership failures, institutional weaknesses, corruption, policy inconsistency, inadequate infrastructure, insecurity and over-dependence on raw material exports. Jonathan challenged Nigeria to learn from countries such as South Korea, India and Singapore, which had made remarkable advancement in industrialisation, technology, education, healthcare and human development. He noted that Nigeria’s enormous human and natural resources should have translated into comparable levels of development, questioning the obstacles that had continued to constrain the country’s potential. item.title: Nigerian Mission hits back at Magwenya, insists Ramaphosa intervened
item.description: The Nigerian High Commission in South Africa has renewed its defence of newly accredited High Commissioner, Chief Femi Fani-Kayode, insisting that President Cyril Ramaphosa personally intervened in the controversy surrounding the presentation of his diplomatic credentials. The mission was responding to South African Presidency spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, who accused Fani-Kayode of lying about Ramaphosa’s intervention following a disagreement over the omission of his address during Friday’s credentials presentation ceremony in Tshwane. In a strongly worded statement posted on X, the Nigerian High Commission accused Magwenya of making provocative and undiplomatic remarks, warning that his comments could undermine diplomatic relations between both countries. The commission said Magwenya had accused Fani-Kayode of lying and disgracing Nigeria barely hours after the envoy presented his letters of credence to the South African President. “You are the disgrace and no-one else. Outside of that your insolence and ignorance knows no bounds. You are bringing your nation into disrepute and wilfully and purposely burning the bridge of peace and reconciliation. That is a matter of concern to us,” the mission said. The controversy followed the apparent disruption of the South African Presidency’s YouTube livestream around the time Fani-Kayode was due to present his letters of credence to Ramaphosa. The broadcast subsequently resumed when the South African President was addressing the ambassadors. Fani-Kayode, who was the last diplomat to present his credentials, had expressed displeasure over the omission of his address from the ceremony. He said he subsequently spoke with Ramaphosa, who apologised and assured him that everything was fine. However, Magwenya disputed the Nigerian envoy’s account, prompting the Nigerian mission to insist that the South African President intervened to resolve the disagreement. The commission also recalled an earlier controversy in which Magwenya reportedly described concerns expressed by President Bola Tinubu and Ghanaian President John Mahama over xenophobia and Afrophobia in South Africa as fake news. It said Nigeria had ignored the earlier remarks but questioned why Magwenya would publicly describe its newly accredited envoy as a liar. “Did you really expect him to simply stomach your ill manners and keep quiet? If so you have misunderstood the character and nature of the Nigerian. We cannot be easily cowed,” the statement added. The mission further disclosed that several people, including newly accredited ambassadors from other countries, witnessed the proceedings and expressed displeasure over what transpired. It also claimed to possess a full video recording of the proceedings after the official photographs were taken, adding that it could release the footage if authorised to do so. item.title: Netanyahu says only unity government can guarantee Israel’s security
item.description: Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, as well as his vow to eliminate the threat from Iran. A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”. He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel “as a state for the Jewish people”. It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”. With backing from 67 lawmakers following last month’s election, Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election. Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the centre to the right, while excluding the Arab parties. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere”. But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday. item.title: ‘Obi ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‌⁠‌‌​is incorruptible,’ says Kwankwaso
item.description: The vice presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has described the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as incorruptible. Kwankwaso made the declaration on Saturday at the 5th convocation ceremony of the Skyline University of Nigeria in Kano. Kwankwaso said the attribute is key and needed in governance of the nation. “One thing I noted in the last few months that we have been working together is that Peter Obi is incorruptible. He’s not somebody that you can go and start thinking of corruption around him, and that is very key in governance in this country,” he said. Kwankwaso pledged that an NDC-led administration would prioritise free education to ensure that no child was denied access to schooling due to financial constraints. “We have so much in common, especially in the issue of education. We believe that together it will be extremely difficult to see how any child will go around in this part of the country or elsewhere begging for what to eat. “In other words, we are working towards free education to ensure that our children are not denied going to school because the parents cannot afford to pay school fees or other expenses. In his remarks, Obi pledged to revive moribund industries in Kano to stimulate economic activities and create employment opportunities. He described Kano as central to Nigeria’s economic development, saying efforts to rebuild the country’s economy must begin with the state. “If we want to fix the North and Nigeria, we must start from Kano. This town represents the soul of Nigeria,” he said. Obi urged the graduates to embrace entrepreneurship, noting that small businesses play a critical role in employment generation and economic growth. item.title: Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The Hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked families affected by the deadly attacks in Anguwan Rukuba , in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State that left many killed and several injured in March 2026, to forgive him for not visiting the communities. ﻿ Tinubu spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally in Jos on Saturday. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport. Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland. But I saw the devastation; I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people. “But since then, that has changed; we are forging together. He, however, assured residents that their communities would be rebuilt for those displaced to return home. Tinubu said too many lives had been lost to attacks in Plateau since 2001. He condoled with families who have lost loved ones to such attacks. Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), called for unity, saying speaking different languages should not lead to divisions. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau. “What we should be getting is prosperity, not havoc, not crisis. Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people up from penury to prosperity. “One thousand forest guards are undergoing training right now. You will feel them; you will see them. You will feel secure in your villages and communities,” he added. The President also said the surveillance cameras had been procured as promised. Tinubu assured the residents that his government his working to ease their suffering. A deadly attack in Anguwan Rukuba, in Jos North Local Government Area of the state in March, 2026, left at least 20 people killed and many others injured. On April 2, Tinubu met with the affected families at the Jos Airport, where he condoled with them and assured them that such an incident would not recur. ﻿ The President was criticised for not visiting the affected communities, but his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga , said that said the visit was affected by a scheduled meeting with the President of Chad.
